verdict_reason: No information leaks on any error path, but the RuntimeException catch-all turns a malformed JSON body into a 500 and the camelCase problem fields contradict the still-snake_case locked contract.

todos.issue: The RuntimeException catch-all swallows Spring's own runtime client-error exceptions: HttpMessageNotReadableException extends NestedRuntimeException, and spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled is not set anywhere in src/main/resources, so Spring's ProblemDetailsExceptionHandler is not registered — a POST/PUT with a truncated or absent JSON body returns 500 internal-error (logged at ERROR with a full stack trace) instead of the contract's 400 bad-request, exactly the fall-through the new handleTypeMismatch handler was added to close.
todos.fix: Add an @ExceptionHandler(HttpMessageNotReadableException.class) returning the bad-request problem (same shape as handleTypeMismatch), plus an IT posting a malformed body; consider narrowing the catch-all or setting spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled.

todos.issue: The handler emits camelCase problem fields (traceId property, errors keyed by the Java field name e.g. addressLine1) but the in-repo docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml at this commit still declares trace_id and 'Map of snake_case wire field name -> list of messages' (keys 'address_line_1, never addressLine1'), so the declared source of truth contradicts the shipped wire; OperatorComplianceIT's divergence gate only compares path sets, HTTP methods and operationIds, so the drift passes CI unnoticed.
todos.fix: Update the Problem/ValidationProblem schemas, the info description and the ValidationProblemExample/TypeChangeProblemExample in docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml to camelCase (cv-001), and extend the divergence gate to compare component-schema property names, not just operationIds.
